title: MZ Playing a sound effect disregarding se volume in settings

posts.author: Tloz
posts.body:
Hi guys.
I'm trying to play a sound effect at a random volume (stored in variable 4) using a script call that looks like that:
JavaScript:
AudioManager.playSe({name: `$name`, pan: 0, pitch: 50, volume: $gameVariables.value(4)});
My issue is that this volume is then modified in regard to the SE Volume in the settings. How do I bypass that setting to make sure that my sound effect will be played at the same volume no matter what the setting is?
Thanks

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:

While it is possible to change the values of the settings midgame within the ConfigManager to do that, i strongly suggest against it. Presumably, the player set their sound effect volume level, and between game settings, the operating system settings, and the actual physical setup, theres no knowing how loud youll be making those sounds

posts.author: Tloz
posts.body: It's not gonna be over the 100% of MV, so the OS settings and the physical setup won't be an issue if the rest of the game is not an issue when I don't change the setting, my SE won't be louder than the rest of the game.

posts.author: Eliaquim
posts.body:
Hi there!
If you want to preserve the previous settings of the player, you can do something like that:
JavaScript:
const oldVolume = ConfigManager.seVolume
ConfigManager.seVolume = XX //(Replace with a number from 0 to 100)
AudioManager.playSe({name: `$name`, pan: 0, pitch: 50, volume: $gameVariables.value(4)});
ConfigManager.seVolume = oldVolume
I think this can work on a script call. I just not sure if when changing the volume back to the old value so quickly, the current SE that is playing will also change it's volume.

The difference is that one is the player preference that is saved. The other is the actual volume while the game is playing:
ConfigManager.seVolume is the player’s saved setting.
it's on the options menu. Changing it updates the preference, but it doesn’t directly control the volume I think.
AudioManager._seVolume is the actual volume used .
This is the value the RPG Maker uses when playing a sound effect. I think, changing it affects the volume right away. But it is not saved.
Normally, RPG Maker copies the value from ConfigManager.seVolume into AudioManager._seVolume when the options change. So I guess is even best if you use the AudioManager._seVolume instead.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
To clarify, I do not read anyone as attacking you, but instead suggesting that ignoring options that players set is really kind of a no-no that might infuriate your players. You were still provided an answer regardless, as we also understand it's your game.
Tloz said:
Are you angry at a game that dims the light (let say because it's night) after it made you set your screen lighting at the beginning of the game?
Click to expand...
It depends on the situation, this is sort of an apples-to-oranges comparison, but depending on how dark the night is; yes. But the truth is that it's not changing the option when it goes night. The gamma value is still the same. It's not ignoring the option that's been set, it's simply a different lighting situation.
Tloz said:
I have a sound based bard character and I want to make sound based mechanics and gameplay.
Click to expand...
Then instead it might be better if you had a separate sound slider for just the bard. That way the player could turn down SE but leave the bard volume at a respectable level. That's a little bit more complicated, but not impossible. I think this option would be far more respectful of your players.
The problem is that you have no sense of what the player's system volume is at. Just because you don't exceed RM's 100% volume, doesn't mean it isn't loud.
Depending on the type of content on my computer, Youtube I typically keep the system volume at around 32 for a comfortable listening volume. Games tend to have quite a large variance in their volume range. Some games I have to turn the system volume up to 70.
Now imagine, I start your game, mix the volume sliders to be comfortable, and have my system volume up to 100. Suddenly your SE plays when I turn that down (or even off). It might either be upsetting, or even worse case could cause damage to my own hardware.
I highly suggest you read my topic on loudness in RPG Maker games.
Why is RPG Maker so dang loud? Well, the results are inconclusive.
PREAMBLE So this was sort of inspired by @caethyril and @bgillisp unintentionally. They aren't aware of the thoughts they planted in my head. It started when bg was showing a screenshot of Theme6 in Audacity and I was surprised to see that the wave form had quite a few peaks and valleys. For...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Because the truth is loudness is not the same as volume. Just because the volume is low, doesn't mean we perceive it as quiet.

The difference is that one is the player preference that is saved. The other is the actual volume while the game is playing:

it's on the options menu. Changing it updates the preference, but it doesn’t directly control the volume I think.

Actually, while this explanation of their purpose is broadly correct, there is no difference between them. They are synonyms –
ConfigManager.seVolume
is defined so that reading from it returns the value of
AudioManager._seVolume
, and writing to it updates the value of
AudioManager._seVolume
. There is also
AudioManager.seVolume
which is another synonym for the same thing.
